intended_object: Take a quadratic map Q : M → P and a submodule W that is a complement of the radical rad(Q). The object is the canonical isometry (w, r) ↦ w + r from the orthogonal sum (Q|_W) ⊥ (0 on rad(Q)) onto (M, Q). This is the standard splitting M = W ⊥ rad(Q). I inferred it from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation:
The underlying linear equivalence is `W.prodEquivOfIsCompl Q.radical hW.symm`, which sends (w, r) to w + r. It is bijective because W and rad(Q) are complements.

The map preserves the forms because Q(w + r) = Q(w) whenever r is in the radical. This follows from `mem_radical_iff'`: Q r = 0 and Q(r + n) = Q n for all n. So the map takes Q|_W(w) + 0(r) to Q(w + r), as required.

Generality: the setting is any commutative ring R and arbitrary modules M and P. That matches the generality of Mathlib's `QuadraticMap.radical`. Using `prodEquivOfIsCompl` needs a ring, which the setting has. Nothing is restricted beyond what the construction needs.

I found no Mathlib declaration giving this isometry: `prodEquivOfIsCompl` never appears in Mathlib's QuadraticForm folder. The definition builds the intended object correctly.
